mirk.title: Mirk
mirk.tagline: A lead-generating website and content platform for a metal-processing plant.
mirk.summary: A ground-up rebuild of the company website for a metal supplier and processing plant in Akko — department pages, local-SEO service areas, a CMS-driven blog and case studies, and an admin panel that routes every inquiry to sales.
mirk.role: Design, full-stack development, CMS and SEO
mirk.challenge: The previous WordPress site was slow, hard to update and undersold the plant’s capabilities. Sales needed a reliable source of inbound leads, and the office team needed to publish content without calling a developer.
mirk.solution: I rebuilt the site on Next.js with Sanity as the content studio, PostgreSQL (via Prisma and Supabase) for leads, newsletter and analytics, and SendGrid for transactional email. The visual design was developed together with the client — a light, industrial palette — and every page was built RTL-first and keyboard- and screen-reader-accessible.
highlights: Department and product pages for laser and plasma cutting, bending, rolling and iron sales
Service-area landing pages for local search across the Western Galilee, Haifa and the Krayot
Blog and case studies edited in an embedded Sanity Studio, with draft previews
Admin panel for inquiries, newsletter subscribers, service areas and activity logs
WhatsApp, Waze and click-to-call shortcuts, with email alerts to the sales team
Full accessibility statement; Hebrew-first with an English version
mirk.result: A fast, statically rendered site the client’s team updates on its own, with every inquiry landing in one place. In Google search, impressions grew 41% across consecutive 28-day periods and two branded searches reached an average first position.

alt.full: Full-length capture of the Mirk homepage

digitengo.title: Digitengo
digitengo.tagline: Lead engineer on a multi-tenant AI platform that runs social-media marketing for small businesses.
digitengo.summary: Digitengo writes, schedules and publishes social posts with AI, reports on paid campaigns across Meta and Google Ads, and captures leads — for small businesses and six white-label partner brands. I’ve led its full-stack development since mid-2025.
digitengo.role: Lead full-stack engineer — architecture, features, infrastructure
digitengo.challenge: A fast-growing product originally built by an outside agency: around seventeen Node.js microservices, a Vue front end and Kubernetes infrastructure, with reliability issues and features that had to ship quickly for paying customers and partners.
digitengo.solution: I took over day-to-day engineering across the whole stack — from the Vue app to the services, queues and AWS infrastructure — shipping new product areas while hardening what was already running in production.
highlights: AI post generation and holiday-aware scheduling with OpenAI and Gemini
Paid-campaigns dashboard combining Meta and Google Ads data with leads and revenue into ROI and ROAS
Publishing to Facebook, Instagram and TikTok, plus Meta lead-form capture
White-label tenants on their own subdomains and a public partner API
Cut the onboarding bundle from 2.27 MB to about 0.55 MB gzipped
Hardened the EKS cluster after a node failure and closed a cross-tenant data leak in scheduled jobs
digitengo.result: A more reliable platform that keeps shipping — over 2,600 commits since July 2025 across the front end, services and infrastructure.

alt.full: Digitengo post feed with scheduled AI-generated posts

my-north-food.title: My North Food
my-north-food.tagline: An online store and operations platform for a Galilee food manufacturer.
my-north-food.summary: A food manufacturer operating since 1979 is moving its ordering, deliveries and back office online: a Hebrew storefront with a product catalog and cart, plus dedicated apps for drivers, production stations and management.
my-north-food.challenge: Orders, delivery routes, kitchen tasks and supplier purchasing were managed by phone and on paper. The business needed one system that customers, drivers, kitchen staff and management could each use from their own device.
my-north-food.solution: I’m building a React and Express platform with role-based areas: the public storefront and customer accounts, an admin back office, a driver app, station screens for the kitchen and warehouse, and a management dashboard — all on one shared database.
highlights: Product catalog, cart and order history, with service requests and inquiries
Back office for products, inventory, weekly menus, kashrut certificates and banners
Driver app with delivery lists and digital signatures on handover
Station screens for daily tasks, goods receipt and purchase orders
Management dashboard for orders and weekly planning
AI chat assistant for customer questions
my-north-food.result: In active development — the public site is live and the operational modules are rolling out in stages.

galil-dashboard.title: Field Organizing Dashboard
galil-dashboard.tagline: An internal dashboard that replaced a tangle of spreadsheets for a regional volunteer organization.
galil-dashboard.summary: A Hebrew, sign-in-protected dashboard that tracks every community in the region — local coordinators, key figures and a history of field events — with Excel import and export so the team can keep working the way it’s used to.
galil-dashboard.challenge: Volunteers were coordinating dozens of communities across two regional councils and several cities from shared spreadsheets that were hard to search, easy to break and impossible to keep in sync.
galil-dashboard.solution: I built a secure Next.js app on Supabase and Prisma that imports the existing spreadsheets, groups communities by council, and lets organizers search, sort and edit figures inline — then export any filtered view back to Excel.
highlights: Communities grouped by regional council, with search across names, coordinators and phone numbers
Inline editing of key figures, color-coded against regional averages
Per-community coordinator lists and an event history with participants and speakers
One-click Excel export of any filtered view, plus a two-sheet export per community
Supabase Auth with server-side checks on every page and API route
Import scripts that seeded the database from the organization’s existing spreadsheets
galil-dashboard.result: One source of truth for the field team, built in a few days.

tor-group.title: TOR Group
tor-group.tagline: A corporate website for an investment-fundraising firm focused on emerging markets.
tor-group.summary: A responsive, multi-language corporate site for a financial-services firm specializing in investment fundraising and international bond issuance — with a growth-themed design, service and team pages, and built-in accessibility features.
tor-group.challenge: The firm needed a credible, modern presence to present its services, process and partners to international investors — in more than one language.
tor-group.solution: I designed and built a Next.js site with next-intl for localization, Framer Motion for restrained animation and a contact form wired to email, structured around the firm’s approach, timing and process.
highlights: Service, approach, timing and process sections built around the firm’s pitch
Multi-language routing with next-intl
Glass-style hero and a growth-themed visual language
Contact form with email delivery, plus Google Analytics
tor-group.result: A polished first impression for investor conversations, live at thetorgroup.com.

alt.full: Full-length capture of the TOR Group homepage

reports-manager.title: Reports Manager
reports-manager.tagline: A Windows desktop app that automates complex Excel reporting for a financial-services firm.
reports-manager.summary: An enterprise reporting tool that ingests large Excel workbooks, validates and reconciles the data, and produces finished reports — replacing hours of manual spreadsheet work. Bilingual Hebrew/English interface.
reports-manager.challenge: Analysts were spending hours each cycle copying, checking and reformatting data across large Excel files, and errors were hard to trace.
reports-manager.solution: I built a WPF application on .NET with EPPlus for Excel processing, JWT-secured access and a guided workflow that flags inconsistencies and helps resolve them before reports are generated.
highlights: Batch processing of large Excel workbooks with EPPlus
Automatic error detection with guided resolution
Hebrew/English interface
Secured access with JWT
reports-manager.result: A repeatable, auditable reporting workflow in place of manual spreadsheet work.
